record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. KAISI describes advanced-AI safety research, but no government designation of it was found; the government framework assigns AI-system audits to independent auditors.

check.language_note: The recorded kk queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged. The additional status review searched Kazakh, Russian and English. The Russian ministry briefing and current law were retrieved; the English briefing is a secondary portal account. KAISI was assessed from its previously retained archive copy because fresh access failed. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 4, 5, 6; 7, 8. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The KAISI source access note says that neither the live contents nor the archived snapshot contents were retrieved. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence. That earlier access limitation was resolved for the declared Wayback capture on 17 October 2026, as recorded in the source access note; the earlier attempts to retrieve the original and a text copy did not supply a new readable live copy. The earlier confidence rule remains superseded.
check.governance_note: The primary ministry briefing and current AI Law were retrieved in Russian. They describe regulation, data governance and independent auditing. They do not identify a national designation as an institute for the safety of advanced models. KAISI's current live pages remain unavailable; its retained archive of its own website describes the research function. The recorded government-source and language evidence supports a bounded medium-confidence finding without treating a missing designation as evidence of absence.

record.notes:
kaisi.kz uses the name 'Kazakhstan AI Safety Institute' and describes research on the safety of advanced models; no national government designation was found. The AI Law (November 2025) provides for audits of AI systems by independent auditors.

The ministry's 14 October briefing was retrieved directly in Russian, alongside the English account on memleket.kz and the current Russian AI Law. The ministry distinguishes its rules and coordination functions from audits carried out by independent specialists and organisations. This supports keeping the ministry department as a related body. KAISI's retained archive describes research on the safety of advanced models and risk mitigation, but no national government designation was found in Kazakh, Russian or English searches. Its live and about pages could not be read reliably. The earlier private non-profit description and staff range were not reverified; the retained home-page copy does not itself establish them. These limits leave the KAISI designation question open.

The KazNIC registry record retrieved on 21 October 2026 showed the status server hold and registration expiry on 1 October 2026. On 2 November 2026 the same registry lookup stated that kaisi.kz does not exist in the registry, and www.kaisi.kz did not resolve. This does not establish whether KAISI still operates or has moved; its government designation remains unverified.

next_check.reason: Check whether KAISI still operates or has moved now that the KazNIC registry no longer lists kaisi.kz (2 November 2026); check whether Kazakhstan's AI initiative for the December 2026 G20 summit or AI Development Council proposals name a body to evaluate advanced models.

closest_body.name: Kazakhstan AI Safety Institute (KAISI)
closest_body.note: The retained website archive presents KAISI as an institute researching advanced-AI capabilities and behaviour and testing risk mitigations. No government assignment was identified. Existence and function are self-described; the live home and about pages could not be reverified. Harvard's Health Systems Innovation Lab lists the Kazakhstan AI Safety Institute as the Astana hub of its 2026 hackathon, scheduled for 10 and 11 April 2026. Whether KAISI still operates after its domain was removed from the registry (by 2 November 2026) is unconfirmed.

claims.text: It says it creates "tools for safe model control and evaluation" to make advanced AI systems more transparent, reliable and aligned with human intentions.
It says its policy research explores how governance frameworks, regulatory approaches and international cooperation can ensure the safe and beneficial deployment of advanced AI systems.
It says it investigates how neural representations emerge and interact, applying techniques such as "activation steering, adversarial robustness analysis, and mechanistic interpretability".
